description:
## What the code does

At crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:33-35:

```rust
if let Some(sd) = show_details {
    args["showDetails"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(sd);
}
```

This is the only place in the crate that constructs a JSON boolean via the explicit `serde_json::Value::Bool(_)` variant. Every other bool insertion uses `.into()`:

- calendar.rs:127 — `args["onDestroyRemoveEvents"] = flag.into();`
- event.rs:44 — `args["expandRecurrences"] = v.into();`
- event.rs:47 — `args["reducedParticipants"] = v.into();`
- event.rs:50 — `args["fetchCalendars"] = v.into();`
- event.rs:185 — `args["expandRecurrences"] = er.into();`

## What idiomatic Rust would do

The `From<bool> for serde_json::Value` impl is exactly `|b| Value::Bool(b)`. `.into()` is the idiomatic conversion call — type-inferred, less ceremony, matches the other five sites.

## Why it matters

Pure local-consistency improvement; no behavioural difference. Flagged as opinion because the explicit-variant form is defensible on its own (clippy doesn't warn on it). The reason to fix is cookie-cutter consistency: a reader who skimmed the other five sites and then hit principal_availability.rs:34 will spend a second wondering whether the explicit variant is doing something different (it isn't).

Note: this is calendars-internal divergence, not a divergence from the canonical mail-client. mail-client doesn't have a `Principal/getAvailability` analog so there's no canonical reference; the comparison is within the crate.

## Fix shape

One-line change at principal_availability.rs:34:

```rust
-    args["showDetails"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(sd);
+    args["showDetails"] = sd.into();
```

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/principal_availability.rs:33-35 (divergent)
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/calendar.rs:126-128 (canonical idiom within the same crate)
- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/event.rs:43-51 (three more canonical idiom sites)
title: principal_get_availability uses Value::Bool(sd) where same crate elsewhere uses sd.into()
